Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this on. We need to lock the acceptance gates and a firm cutover window for the Hosted->Dedicated migration tied to our committed capacity. Our primary asks:

- Clear throughput/latency acceptance criteria (95th pctl token latency, sustained RPS)
- A short stress run that mirrors production traffic (can we mirror for 90m?)
- Any expected changes to caching/KV behavior that could affect observed latency
- A short blackout / rollback window we can rely on if anything looks off

Can you share a proposed validation schedule and who from Redwood will be on the call? I attached our internal ops map as a reference.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations, NovaHealth

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Draft plan below (high level) — happy to iterate:

1) Preflight (Tue 2026-09-21):
   - Verify reserved token rate and concurrency settings (Redwood Dedicated pool RDW-NH-01)
   - Confirm model variant and quantization profile pinned for cutover
   - Smoke: 15m of traffic at baseline (no KV cache priming)

2) Throughput validation (Wed 2026-09-22 AM):
   - 90-minute mirror run using production traffic (sampling 20% to avoid side-effects)
   - Target: sustain 250 requests/sec with 95th pctl token latency < 180ms
   - Observability: token-level latency traces, per-route cost and per-model CPU/GPU util

3) Cutover (Wed 2026-09-22 16:00-17:00 PDT):
   - 60-minute monitored switchover with a 30-minute rollback window
   - Post-cutover sanity: KV cache hit-rate, tail latency, billing/usage delta check

Attached: migration map + quick acceptance checklist.

Questions for your ops team:
- Are you comfortable with a sampled mirror (20%) or do you need full traffic mirroring?
- Any blackout constraints for 09/22 16:00 PST?

Ben and Grace are looped for commercial and CS-side readiness. Karthik will own throughput validation with infra.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite when we confirm the final window.

--
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Elena / team — confirmed. Final operational plan and handback steps below:

Preflight (09/21 EOD call):
- Participants: Rachel (AM), Karthik (Infra lead), Grace (CS), Nova ops engineering
- Deliverables: runbook walk, test token list, monitoring dashboards (links included)

Throughput validation (09/22 09:30-11:00 PDT):
- We'll perform a 90-minute mirror run at full traffic as requested. Redwood infra will mirror traffic into Dedicated pool RDW-NH-01 with isolated routing.
- Instrumentation: token-level latency traces, GPU util, per-route error rates, prefix/KV cache hit rates.
- Acceptance gate: 95th pctl token latency < 180ms AND error rate < 0.5% for primary routes.

Cutover window (09/22 16:00 PDT):
- Plan: Update routing policy to point NovaHealth production traffic at RDW-NH-01. If rollback needed, routing policy fallback to Hosted pool within 30 minutes.
- On-call: Karthik will execute rollback; Grace to confirm CS notification to product teams; Ben to confirm billing transition meeting post-acceptance.

Post-cutover (09/22 17:00-18:00 PDT):
- 60-minute observation and final sign-off. If all gates pass, we'll issue formal handback notice and execute Docusign acceptance. Link included below.
